title: APAC Gold Market Insights: Gold allocation in different Chinese economic cycles
gist: The World Gold Council argues that China's prolonged structural transition (real estate weakness vs 14% high-tech value-add growth) keeps it in a slowdown-type cycle, where back-tests of a 35/55/10 pension-style portfolio favour a higher RMB gold allocation (~21% in slowdown, 28% in stagnation vs 16% strategic, 5–11% in good times); Q3 2026 Chinese retail demand rose to 192t and the PBoC added 63t, its strongest quarter since Q3 2022.

insights.claim: China's growth slowdown reflects a transition from traditional sector-led growth to new-tech-led growth, with diminishing contribution from old engines like real estate while new sectors are not yet large enough to provide broad-based momentum.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Expect a prolonged low-growth, low-rate China regime rather than a quick cyclical rebound.
insights.locator: China’s economy is passing through an extended period

insights.claim: Chinese high-tech sector value-add rose 14% y/y in January–September 2026 versus 5% across all industries, while residential home starts and sales kept falling.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The bifurcation favours Chinese tech exposure over property-linked assets.
insights.locator: For instance, the real estate sector

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects China may stay in its current slowdown-type economic cycle for a while amid the ongoing transition, which argues for a higher gold allocation in Chinese portfolios.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Supports sustained Chinese investment demand for gold while the regime persists.
insights.quote: we may stay in the current cycle for a while

insights.claim: In China's slowdown phase — lower rates, tepid borrowing — local equities typically weaken while defensive assets such as government bonds and gold outperform.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: In slowdown regimes, overweight CGBs and gold vs CSI300.

insights.claim: The WGC classifies Chinese economic cycles using loan growth and the 7-day interbank pledged repo rate versus their past-four-quarter averages: slowdown (both below), recovery (loans above, repo below), expansion (both above), stagnant (loans below, repo above).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A simple, replicable regime filter for tactical China allocation.
insights.locator: Chart 3 note: Economic cycles are determined

insights.claim: RMB-denominated gold has delivered positive average returns in all four Chinese economic cycles, compounding about 9% annually over the past 20 years and outpacing other assets.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold is an all-weather asset for RMB investors, not just a crisis hedge.
insights.locator: Gold, in RMB, however delivers strong returns

insights.claim: Gold's cycle-robust returns stem from its dual nature as consumer good and investment asset (cyclical jewellery/tech demand vs counter-cyclical investor demand) and from a globally diversified demand base not tied to any single economy.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Demand stability explains why gold works across regimes — the thesis rests on breadth of buyers.
insights.locator: It is mainly driven by two of gold’s distinctive aspects

insights.claim: The correlation between RMB gold and Chinese equities turns negative during economic stress, aiding diversification, and flips positive in prosperity, preserving portfolio upside.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold offers asymmetric correlation for China equity holders — hedge when needed, participate when not.

insights.claim: Back-testing a hypothetical Chinese basic pension portfolio of 35% equities, 55% bonds and 10% cash shows a 16% gold allocation maximises the marginal improvement in Sharpe ratio across all economic cycles.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: 16% is the WGC's strategic anchor for Chinese multi-asset portfolios — far above typical institutional holdings.
insights.locator: Back-testing historical data of a hypothetical Chinese basic pension portfolio

insights.claim: A purely Sharpe-maximising Chinese portfolio since 2004 would require a gold allocation of more than 50% (58% in the WGC chart), which the WGC deems unrealistic, so it targets marginal Sharpe improvement instead.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold's exceptional RMB returns since 2004 bias naive optimisers; marginal-Sharpe is a more practical sizing rule.
insights.locator: We focus on marginal improvement rather than the absolute Sharpe ratio

insights.claim: To maximise marginal Sharpe improvement, a Chinese portfolio needs about 21% gold in slowdowns and 28% in stagnant periods.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Under the WGC's regime view, current Chinese conditions imply gold weights well above strategic.

insights.claim: In Chinese recoveries and expansions, gold allocations of about 11% and 5% respectively preserve at least 98% upside return participation while still improving the portfolio's Sharpe ratio.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Cut gold weight when credit and rates turn up — gold costs return in booms.

insights.claim: Across rolling horizons of the past 5, 10, 15, 20 and 22 years, the gold allocation maximising Sharpe improvement for a Chinese portfolio ranged between 9% and 16%, reducing regime-selection bias in the result.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The 9–16% range is robust to sample choice, strengthening the strategic case.
insights.locator: In addition to economic cycles, we also back tested

insights.claim: Chinese retail gold demand totalled 192t in Q3 2026, up 24% q/q and 12% y/y.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Robust Chinese retail demand underpins the gold bid.
insights.locator: The gold demand picture in China during Q3

insights.claim: Chinese bar and coin investment was 79t in Q3 2026 (+7% y/y, -26% q/q), well above the 10-year Q3 average of 65t, while jewellery consumption rose 30% q/q to 66t but was down 22% y/y.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Investment demand is the growth engine; high prices continue to suppress jewellery.
insights.locator: Bar and coin investment stayed robust at 79t

insights.claim: Chinese gold ETFs saw 27t of inflows in Q3 2026, reversing a 22t Q2 loss, and industrial demand held stable at 20t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Return of ETF inflows signals renewed institutional/retail financial demand.
insights.locator: local gold ETFs saw inflows of 27t

insights.claim: The PBoC reported adding 63t of gold in Q3 2026, its strongest quarter since Q3 2022, lifting year-to-date purchases to 103t and official holdings to 2,410t, or 8.5% of total reserves.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Accelerating official Chinese buying is a structural price support; reserves share still low vs peers implies runway.
insights.locator: The PBoC reported an addition of 63t
